extracted.intended_audience: Government of India Departments / Ministries drafting legislation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Indian Government Departments/Ministries on procedures and minimum standards for publishing draft legislation, conducting pre-legislative consultations, documenting feedback, and ensuring legal vetting before Cabinet and Parliament. Focuses on transparency, stakeholder outreach, and procedural checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive publication of proposed legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Department/Ministry shall proactively publish the proposed legislations both on the internet as also through other means; the detailed modalities of such publication may be worked out by the Department/Ministry concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication should be proactive and may use internet plus other media; departments may determine detailed modalities appropriate to their context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish draft or essential information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department/Ministry concerned should publish/place in public domain the draft legislation or at least the information that may inter alia include brief justification for such legislation, essential elements of the proposed legislation, its broad financial implications, and an estimated assessment of the impact of such legislation on environment, fundamental rights, lives and livelihoods of the concerned/affected people, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If full draft is not possible, at minimum provide justification, key elements, financial implications and estimated impact assessments addressing environment, fundamental rights, and effects on lives and livelihoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum public availability period
rubrics_metrics.description: Such details may be kept in the public domain for a minimum period of thirty days for being proactively shared with the public in such manner as may be specified by the Department/Ministry concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set public comment/availability period at least 30 days; exact manner/timing may be specified by the department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted publicity for affected groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Where such legislation affect specific group of people, it may be documented and disclosed through print or electronic media or in such other manner, as may be considered necessary to give wider publicity to reach the affected people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use additional outreach channels (print, electronic, other) as necessary to ensure notice reaches specifically affected populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include prior-publication provision in new principal legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: As a matter of practice, a provision regarding the previous publication of rules should be made in all new principal legislations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft principal legislation should contain an explicit clause requiring prior publication of subordinate rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory note in plain language
rubrics_metrics.description: Every draft legislation or rules, placed in public domain through pre-legislative process should be accompanied by an explanatory note explaining key legal provisions in a simple language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accompany drafts with plain-language explanatory notes summarizing and clarifying key legal provisions for non-specialist stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish summary of feedback/comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary of feedback/comments received from the public/other stakeholders should also be placed on the website of the Department/Ministry concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departments must post summaries of public and stakeholder feedback to their websites so the record of inputs is publicly accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional stakeholder consultations with departmental discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department/Ministry concerned might, in addition to placing the proposal in public domain, also hold consultations with all stakeholders. However, the degree of participation and mode of consultations may be decided by the Department/Ministry concerned and may vary according to the nature of the subject and the potential impact on those who will be affected by such legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departments encouraged to hold consultations but retain discretion over scope and format; tailor participation level to subject matter and likely impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer Bill to Ministry of Law and Justice for vetting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bill should be referred to the Ministry of Law and Justice for inter-ministerial vetting after consultations are over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send draft Bill to Ministry of Law and Justice post-consultation for legal vetting and inter-ministerial coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministry of Law and Justice to ensure compliance with PLCP
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ministry of Law and Justice shall also, at the time of examination of the draft legislation or rules, ensure that the concerned Department/Ministry has complied with the process of pre-legislative consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal vetting must include verification that pre-legislative consultation steps were followed; MoLJ to check procedural compliance as part of examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include summary of feedback and departmental response in Cabinet note
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department/Ministry concerned should include a brief summary of the feedback received from stakeholders (including Government Departments and the public) along with its response in the note for the Cabinet along with the draft legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cabinet submission must attach a concise summary of stakeholder feedback plus the department's responses to those points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place pre-legislative process summary before Parliamentary Standing Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary of pre-legislative process should also be placed before the Department Related Parliamentary Standing Committee by the Department/Ministry concerned when the proposed legislation is brought to the Parliament and is referred to the Standing Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a Bill goes to Parliament and is referred to the relevant Standing Committee, provide the committee with the pre-legislative consultation summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record reasons if consultations not feasible/desirable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Department/Ministry concerned is of the view that it is not feasible or desirable to hold pre-legislative consultation as detailed above, it may record the reasons in the note for the Cabinet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a department opts out of pre-legislative consultation, document and justify the decision in the Cabinet note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify existing procedural manuals/instructions as required
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manual for Parliamentary Procedures in the Government of India, and the instructions issued by the Cabinet Secretariat on writing Cabinet Notes may, to the extent required, be suitably modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update internal manuals and Cabinet Note drafting instructions to reflect and operationalize the pre-legislative consultation policy where needed.
